minutes.headline: Capital Planning ranked its FY25 capital requests by average score; final vote on the list is set for Thursday.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed members' individual rankings of capital requests, sorted by average, after public comment from the Parks Commission chair on Marshall Pond and Wallace Park. Debate centered on the DPW's second front-end loader, infrastructure and storm water versus equipment, and school window safety film. One member's rankings were still missing; members may revise rankings by Thursday, when a final vote on the prioritized list is planned. Minutes of the prior meeting were taken up with a motion.

public_comment.topic: Parks Commission chair (Lockwood, 91 Main Street) responded to prior comments on Marshall Pond weed/pond remediation, recreation use, and Wallace Park repair priority.
Follow-up on Marshall Pond permit expiring, and a request for a running multi-year total of capital spending by department, including cemetery.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of November 20, 2023 (motion and second heard; vote 'I' called, no opposition heard).

budget_items.topic: Cumulative cost at the halfway point of the ranked list
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair put the running cost at the halfway line of the ranked list, with a figure the captions render roughly.

budget_items.topic: DPW second front-end loader with plow
budget_items.what_was_said: A member objected that a second loader expands the fleet and its upkeep; others defended it as a department need with a long expected life.
Large health insurance increases were noted as pressure on the budget and funding for the capital plan.
A project for the field ranked fairly high; equity of access was debated.
A member asked about past capital funding levels and a loss of funding in this year was mentioned.
The preliminary capital plan is presented mid-January and the preliminary budget in February.

budget_items.topic: DPW equipment spending in recent years
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled substantial approved DPW equipment spending over four years.

decisions.decision: Members may revise and resubmit rankings by Thursday; the chair will acknowledge each by email.
Next meeting Thursday at 6 to finalize the prioritized list and take the final vote; it then goes to the town manager.
Tied items may be ordered by the committee as a preference; the town manager retains discretion.
A second-half look at longer-term department plans is planned for spring.

what_happened.line: Capital Planning reviewed members' rankings of FY25 capital requests sorted by average score, and took no vote on the list.
Members may revise and resubmit rankings by Thursday; the chair will acknowledge each revision by email.
Debate on the DPW's second front-end loader ended without a resolution; one member objected that it expands the fleet and its upkeep.
The committee will meet Thursday at 6 to finalize the prioritized list and take the final vote, after which it goes to the town manager.
Tied items may be ordered by the committee as a preference, but the town manager retains discretion.

why_it_matters: The ranked list is the committee's advice on which vehicles, equipment, field and building projects come first in the FY25 capital plan, and the town manager is not bound to follow it.
Items that make the list can later appear as capital articles residents are asked to vote on at town meeting.
